summary: Clearwater County lookout: a 1921 log platform burned in 1961, and a 50-ft L-4 tower moved in from Indian Grave in 1962 was gone by 1983 or 1985, leaving foundation piers.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 50-foot treated timber tower (1962 replacement), after a 1921 log platform
facts.status_note: The 1962 replacement tower was gone by 1983 or 1985, depending on the source. The register says concrete foundation piers remain.

staffing.status: One known staff member: Roger C Garrett, 1963, per Idaho Fire Lookouts

access.note: Reached by Forest Road 500 from Highway 12, per SummitPost. No closure notice found in our sources.

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts tags the site Drive-Up. SummitPost calls the access road very narrow. No tower stands there to climb.

events.note: The original log platform burned in a forest fire
A 50-foot L-4 tower moved from Indian Grave Lookout replaced the platform
Roger C Garrett listed as known staff, per Idaho Fire Lookouts
Idaho Fire Lookouts and the Idaho page citing Kresek date destruction to 1983. Firelookout.com says it stood on site until 1983. The register gives 1985.
The register says the replacement tower burned in a 1985 forest fire
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register, nominated by Roger Lord

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the replacement tower burned in 1985 and was removed that year. Firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the Idaho page citing Kresek date its loss to 1983. We could not settle which is right, so the story reports both.

Our records hold two coordinate pairs about 1 km apart. The register's coordinates are used here. SummitPost describes a summit about two miles from the lake that some call the lookout site, so the exact spot is not settled.

notes_for_editor: Fate date (1983 vs 1985) is unresolved; a newspaper or Forest Service record would settle it. The access note relies on a climbing site (SummitPost) and no Forest Service closure check was made. The site's location is uncertain: two coordinate pairs about 1 km apart, and SummitPost puts the lookout on a summit two miles from the lake. The brief's name has a typo ('SIte'). No new photo with a usable URL was found; the register credits Roger Lord for its photo.
